title: USTC: Principles and Techniques of Compiler

unit.title: Lexical Analysis as a Tested Software Contract
unit.scope: A bounded, self-contained preparation unit on specifying, implementing, and testing a small C++ lexer before using a lexer generator or the unavailable official lab framework.
unit.audience: A student strong in algorithms who is developing production-oriented software-engineering habits.
prerequisite_assumptions: Comfort with asymptotic reasoning, finite-state processes, and basic data structures
Ability to compile and test a small C++17 project
No prior compiler implementation experience is required
learning_objectives: Turn a lexical specification into an explicit token and diagnostic contract
Implement maximal-munch scanning with correct keyword, operator, comment, and position behavior
Separate reusable lexer logic from a command-line adapter
Build deterministic unit and integration tests that expose boundary failures
Record design decisions and reproducible evidence without overstating completion
learner_deliverables: A dependency-free C++17 lexer library and minilex command-line program
Written responses to the comprehension prompts

unit_completion_requires: A validator-controlled clean build and automated test run succeed
Independent review finds the implementation, tests, design record, and comprehension responses satisfactory
completion_policy.validation_authority: Only an independent validator controlled by the worker harness may mark this unit complete.
completion_policy.course_completion_rule: This kickoff is only the first bounded unit. Completing it never demonstrates completion of the USTC course, its six described labs, or the wider topics in the catalog. Later units must be separately sourced, prepared, attempted, and validated.
completion_policy.no_inferred_credit: Catalog descriptions, linked resources, time spent, and prose claims do not count as completion evidence.
